newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef traded lower on fairly good demand and moderate to heavy offerings, USDA said. Good retail demand was noted for upcoming holiday and first of the month featuring needs.

Chuck and round cuts traded lower early in the week as inventories were rather burdensome. However, some Choice chuck cuts ended the trading period on a firm undertone as export demand helped support these items.
Rib and loin cuts traded uneven as Choice product was generally steady while Select product traded lower as supplies of these cuts have increased in recent weeks.
Closely trimmed items traded lower on good demand with the most pressure on the Select cuts. Beef trimmings were lower on light to moderate demand and moderate to heavy offerings.

Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were generally steady on light to moderate demand and mostly moderate offerings. These items ended the trading period on a weak undertone as demand was for the upcoming holiday was disappointing

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal 1.00 to 3.00 lower; Select and Choice chuck primal .50 to 2.00 lower; Select and Choice round primal 2.00 to 3.00 lower; Select and Choice loin primal steady to 3.00 lower; Closely trimmed items .50 to 2.00 lower; Beef trimmings 4.00 lower; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items generally steady.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn .86 at 105.96; 700/850 Dn .90 at 106.07; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 2.32 at 98.62; 700/850 Dn 2.21 at 98.11.

COW and BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT Demand for lean boneless beef continues to be light as supplies of finished product and alternative beef grinding material remained plentiful. As a result, lean boneless beef traded lower again this week.

However, the cow carcass market was steady to firm on moderate demand and light to moderate offerings. The cow cuts complex was steady to firm, with the exception of the 100% lean flats/eyes and supermill which moved at weaker prices on light to moderate demand and offerings.

Utility carcasses steady to firm; Cutter not tested; 90% boneless beef 1.50-2.00 lower; 85% 2.50 lower; 75% lower; 65% 3.00-4.50 lower. The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, May 15, 1997 was estimated at 77.37 per cwt., down .71 from a week ago Friday.
